A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 10-page versions of FloVD, with matching methods and principal experiments. Neither contains appendices or the separately referenced supplement. V2 redirects some analyses to that unavailable supplement, limiting verification of whether they were relocated unchanged.

before.justification: V1 reports original camera-control and video-quality experiments in Tables 1–2, ablations in Tables 3–4, and qualitative application results.

after.justification: V2 retains original camera-control and video-quality results in Tables 1–2, component ablations in Table 3, and qualitative application results.

M1.justification: The camera-flow generation, object motion synthesis model, flow integration, and flow-conditioned video synthesis model remain unchanged. Sections 3–4 retain the same architectures, training stages, and objectives.

E1.justification: Both versions use the internal full and curated datasets, RealEstate10K, and four Pexels evaluation subsets. Video editing and dolly-zoom demonstrations are retained; moving the dolly-zoom example into Figure 1 adds no task coverage.

E2.justification: MotionCtrl and CameraCtrl remain the evaluated external comparators in the corresponding quantitative and qualitative comparisons. Newly cited related work is not added to these experiments.

E3.justification: The reported training budgets, batch sizes, 14-frame outputs, 320 × 576 resolution, evaluation sample counts, seven camera trajectories, and metrics are unchanged. Omitted sampling-strategy results do not establish a revision to the retained experimental settings.

E4.justification: V2 retains the component ablations and flow-conditioned synthesis analysis, but no longer directly presents v1’s QTS-versus-EDM camera-control study or its dedicated discussion. It also omits the EDM component-ablation rows. References to supplemental Tables S1–S2 suggest relocation, but their contents cannot be verified.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The point-estimate reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the retained Table 3 rows have identical values. V2 does not reproduce the three EDM rows, including the full-model FVD of 80.74, or Table 4’s EDM camera errors of 1.70°, 0.0983, and 0.1010. This reduces directly available results; it does not establish changed performance or deletion from the unavailable supplement.

T1.justification: The flow-integration equation, flow-embedding definition, and camera-error formulas remain unchanged. Neither version introduces additional propositions, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: optical flow enables training without camera annotations, and the two-stage framework supports accurate camera control with natural object motion.

C2.justification: V2 adds an interpretation connecting MotionCtrl’s artifacts to its worse FID scores. It omits v1’s explicit discussion of the QTS quality-versus-control tradeoff and its explanation involving highly noised training inputs. The physical flow-integration and segmentation limitations remain.

D1.justification: The shortened video-editing description in Section 5.5 removes the application-specific RAFT citation and the named InfEdit editing-tool example. Core implementation settings and training details remain unchanged; no replacement tools or changed procedure are established.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces the object-motion overview with a focused discussion of prior flow-based two-stage synthesis, distinguishing FloVD through camera control and camera/object motion separation. Four references are added, including MoVideo and latent flow diffusion; four are removed, including cINNs, MCVD, sparse-trajectory generation, and InfEdit.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized copyedits, changes related-work headings, shortens analysis and application passages, and adds acknowledgments. The overall section sequence remains intact. Section 5.2 also introduces a near-duplicate paragraph describing the camera-control evaluation protocol.

P2.justification: Figure 1 becomes a full-width teaser incorporating v1’s Figure 10 dolly-zoom example and explanatory graphics. Existing figures and tables are repositioned. Table 3 loses its timestep-strategy column and EDM rows, and Table 4 is no longer displayed in the supplied PDF.

improvement.justification: V2 clarifies its relationship to earlier two-stage methods and improves the introductory illustration, but duplicates protocol prose and provides less directly inspectable sampling analysis and application detail. The principal method and results are unchanged. Because the omitted analyses are redirected to an unavailable supplement, their preservation cannot be checked, and the mixed changes do not establish a reliable overall quality improvement or deterioration.
